claim: Waves 2 and 3 are planned in parallel but depend on each other at compile and test time. Wave 3's Request must return the Method enum owned by wave 2 (req.method(), D-042) and expose matched route params (D-075). Wave 2's automatic responses (404/405+Allow, HEAD without body, OPTIONS 204, 501, 426) can only be exercised through a Response and the in-memory adapter or pipeline that wave 3 owns (D-102, D-108). Neither section owns the dispatcher that connects the router to Request and Response.

claim: D-335 says SSE uses TinyHttpd's event stream, and D-019 forbids patching TinyHttpd. That EventStream cannot produce the wire format that D-326 and D-330 require. startEventStream() hard-codes 'Cache-Control: no-cache' and commits inside the call, so 'no-cache, no-transform' cannot be sent. retry() writes its own 'retry: n' block terminated by a blank line, and send(event,data,id) writes event, id, data, so the single 'event/id/retry/data' event shown in docs/api/sse.md cannot be emitted. The obvious workaround, a hand-rolled chunked stream, keeps the worker inside TinyHttpd's worker budget (no detach), which conflicts with D-336/D-346. TinyHttpd also needs one owner thread per stream blocked in awaitClosed(), which the D-106 SPI extension point has to model.
evidence: TinyHttpd core/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/server/SseStream.java:53 (setHeader Cache-Control no-cache), :72 (commitStreaming inside start), :129-130 (retry offered as separate 'retry: n\n\n'), :89-110 (event,id,data order); http/EventStream.java javadoc (owner thread must call awaitClosed); object.md:458 and docs/api/sse.md:25 (no-cache, no-transform); docs/api/sse.md:57-63 (combined event with retry); design 00.design.md:509, :513, :518.

claim: D-324 raises only maxUpgradedConnections, but other TinyHttpd defaults also block the T26 load test of 100+ WebSocket and SSE connections. maxConnectionsPerAddress=32 applies to every socket, including long-lived ones, and every test client connects from 127.0.0.1. maxEventStreams=64 answers 503 to the 65th SSE stream. maxConnections=128 is below 100 WS + 100 SSE. The test as designed fails against the default adapter configuration.

claim: Parallel waves 6 and 7 write the same files and contracts. Both update docs/api/defaults.md (D-239, D-272 vs D-303, D-339). Both extend the shutdown sequence owned by wave 4 (D-162): temp-file cleanup (D-255) against WS/SSE close and force-close (D-340..D-345). Both need new configuration APIs that touch RestApp or its config classes (static symlink/SPA settings, Origin allowlist, WS/SSE limits), which I-014 forbids outside a serial merge. D-324/D-335 change TinyHttpd builder settings in the adapter core, contradicting D-210's 'without editing the adapter core'.

Several errors that the design routes through NaruServe error handling are actually produced by the TinyHttpd parser or acceptor as prebuilt raw responses, before NaruServe sees the request. These are invalid path/encoded slash/NUL/dot segment (400), header too large (431), request line too long (414), CL+TE conflict (400) and worker queue overflow (503). They never reach onError (D-129), carry no standard JSON body or requestId (D-132, D-135), and produce no access log line (D-173 'exactly one line per HTTP request'). D-134 lists 'worker queue overflow 503' in the JSON mapping, which cannot hold on the TinyHttpd adapter.

claim: TinyHttpd's request parser is stricter than the NaruServe routing items, and it applies before the core runs. It returns 400 for any '.' or '..' segment (not only those that escape the root), for any %2F in any path (so a :param can never hold an encoded '/'), and for raw non-ASCII bytes. Its getPath() also merges '//' segments. The in-memory adapter (D-108) applies only D-051/D-052, so the same request can behave differently on the two adapters, and D-224 runs T07 on both. D-053's switchable '//' policy also needs the adapter to pass getRequestURI() rather than getPath(), otherwise decoding happens twice and contradicts D-051.
evidence: TinyHttpd server/PercentCodec.java:25-53 (decodePath rejects encoded slash, NUL, '.' and '..', merges empty segments), :73-75 (non-ASCII rejected); server/RequestParser.java:30-31 (null path -> 400), :89-93 (path decoded at parse time); http/Request.java:21, :41; design 00.design.md:90-93, :182, :344.

claim: Modules introduced by later waves are missing from the wave-1 module list, so those waves must edit settings.gradle and the root build.gradle that wave 1 owns. This contradicts D-005 (all main dependencies declared up front). The modules are the SLF4J adapter and rotating file logger (wave 4, D-179, with an SLF4J main dependency) and the Logcat Logger artifact (wave 8, D-371). The Logcat module also needs android.jar or an Android plugin, which is at odds with D-025 (root build passes without an Android SDK) unless a compile-only android stub artifact is named.

D-194 requires Map values to round-trip 'unchanged' through req.body and res.json. With the default Gson that D-197 defines (only STRICT and disableJdkUnsafe), decoding into Map or Object turns every JSON number into Double, so {"a":1} comes back as {"a":1.0}. Two implementations could both claim T08: one tests Map<String,String>, the other sets ToNumberPolicy.LONG_OR_DOUBLE.
evidence: design 00.design.md:306 (D-194), :312 (D-197); object.md:1040 (T08 includes Map); object.md:303-304 (default builder); Gson default ObjectToNumberStrategy is ToNumberPolicy.DOUBLE.

claim: Some items sit in sections earlier than the APIs they need. D-068/D-069 (WS route coexistence, 426) are in wave 2, but app.ws registration only exists from wave 4 (D-114) and is specified in wave 7 (D-294). D-117/D-121 (middleware on static and WS-upgrade requests, static fall-through) are in wave 4, before staticFiles (wave 6) and upgrades (wave 7) exist.

D-251 refers to 'the small in-memory limit documented in docs/api/multipart.md', but multipart.md names no value ('한도를 넘으면 예외') and no decision item (D-239) owns choosing it, so the test has no bound to assert.

The design does not say how symlinks are refused on API 21. java.nio.file.Files.isSymbolicLink is API 26+, so detection must use java.io canonical-vs-absolute comparison, per path component. On Android the mount root itself is often reached through a symlink (/sdcard -> /storage/emulated/0), so the root must be canonicalised once, or every file is refused.

If-Modified-Since has one-second resolution, but File.lastModified() has millisecond resolution. Comparing them without truncating mtime to seconds means a file whose mtime has a sub-second part never gets 304.

D-247 allows two multipart parsers: the core parser and TinyHttpd's MultipartReader with its own MultipartLimits. Only T07 is required to run on both adapters (D-224), so limit, header-size and malformed-boundary behaviour (D-233..D-236) may diverge on the parser that is not tested.

Three items own the same (미확정) module-name markers. D-029 (wave 1) removes the #1 markers from README.md, D-230 (wave 5) again replaces the bootstrap and Gson names in README.md, and D-357 (wave 8) does the same for the Kotlin module. This conflicts with I-008 (update docs in the same wave as the change).
